title: Linking Resources
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of linking resources in a browser document.
Apply at least one relevant rule from this lesson to a small HTML example.
Check the result using browser inspection, a validator, or an accessibility checklist.

content.intro: This lesson turns “Linking Resources” into a practical authoring skill. You will work with the <link> element and external resources, understand the choices that matter, and check the result instead of relying on guesswork.
content.why_it_matters: Meaningful structure and metadata make content easier to navigate, understand, share, and maintain across different devices and assistive technologies.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Meaningful structure and metadata make content easier to navigate, understand, share, and maintain across different devices and assistive technologies.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Link relates the document to an external resource, commonly a stylesheet or icon.

items.title: The <link> element and external resources
items.text: Link relates the document to an external resource, commonly a stylesheet or icon.

items.title: Linking stylesheets
items.text: Resolve the URL relative to the current document or base URL. Prefer meaningful link text, test internal paths from each page location, and verify external destinations.

items.title: The rel attribute
items.text: The rel attribute: the relationship between the current document and the destination, often used to add security or meaning.

items.title: The media attribute
items.text: Include the media controls people need and alternatives to important audio or visual information. Check format support, file paths, caption timing, and permission/privacy needs.

items.title: Favicons and icon resources
items.text: Choose resource hints and loading behavior from measurement, not habit. Preserve intrinsic dimensions, avoid lazy-loading content needed immediately, and prioritize only genuinely important resources.

items.title: Alternate language and format links
items.text: Form controls need meaningful labels and names, clear instructions, and constraints that match the data. Treat browser validation as feedback for users, not proof that submitted data is trustworthy.

items.title: Preload, preconnect, and other resource hints at a conceptual level
items.text: Choose resource hints and loading behavior from measurement, not habit. Preserve intrinsic dimensions, avoid lazy-loading content needed immediately, and prioritize only genuinely important resources.

content_blocks.title: Keep in mind
content_blocks.text: Prefer the native semantic element that communicates intent. Do not choose markup solely for its default visual style.

content.task: Create a small HTML example that demonstrates linking resources. Keep the markup minimal, give every element a clear purpose, and inspect the rendered result.
task_acceptance_criteria: Use the relevant concept from Linking Resources.
Keep IDs unique and use valid nesting.
Check the result in a browser and record one finding.
hints: Start with the smallest valid example for linking resources.
Add one element or attribute at a time, then check the result.
Compare the source and rendered DOM if the behavior surprises you.
content.expected_output: The first two links open local pages when those files exist; the fragment link jumps to the Contact section.

troubleshooting.symptom: The expected content does not appear.
troubleshooting.check: Confirm the file was saved with an .html extension and inspect its path and nesting.
Check the resolved URL and confirm the referenced file or external resource exists and allows the request.

troubleshooting.symptom: The page looks correct but the markup may be invalid.
troubleshooting.check: Run the Nu Html Checker and follow its first relevant diagnostic, then validate again.

common_mistakes.why: The default appearance is not the element’s main meaning and can make navigation or maintenance harder.
common_mistakes.fix: Choose the element that matches the content purpose, then use CSS for presentation.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a browser’s recovery means the source is valid
common_mistakes.why: Browsers often recover from malformed markup, which can hide defects and produce unexpected document structure.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the rendered DOM and run a validator against the original source.

common_mistakes.why: Missing files, narrow viewports, keyboard access, invalid input, or other states can expose defects.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the expected state plus one realistic edge case and an accessibility path.

summary: Linking Resources is about expressing document structure or behavior intentionally.

Choose resource hints and loading behavior from measurement, not habit. Preserve intrinsic dimensions, avoid lazy-loading content needed immediately, and prioritize only genuinely important resources.
Verify both markup and behavior; do not infer correctness from appearance alone.
